The Journey • ታሪክ

From the Sacred Highlands of Gojjam to Global Reverence

Born in the picturesque highland town of Chagni, northwestern Ethiopia, Ejigayehu Shibabaw grew up surrounded by the sacred vocal cadences of Ethiopian Orthodox liturgy, traditional wedding bards, and the poetic storytelling of rural Azmaris. Blessed with an astonishing five-octave vocal range, she began singing in early childhood, absorbing the complex modal microtones of Ethiopian vocal expression.

Her artistic path carried her from Addis Ababa to Kenya and eventually to San Francisco and New York, where she met visionary producer and bassist Bill Laswell. In 2001, she released her monumental self-titled international debut on Palm Pictures—an album that stunned the global music landscape. Laswell assembled an unprecedented ensemble including jazz legends Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, Pharoah Sanders, and percussion maestro Zakir Hussain, creating a timeless nexus between ancient Abyssinian scales and contemporary world jazz.

“My voice belongs to the earth of Ethiopia. When I sing, I am not merely delivering notes—I am summoning the prayers of my ancestors, the longing of our mothers, and the unyielding dignity of our people.”

— Gigi (Ejigayehu Shibabaw)

6th-Century Ethiopian Sacred Music St. Yared Signs • የዜማ ምልክቶች

Saint Yared's Musical Notation (የቅዱስ ያሬድ የዜማ ምልክቶች)

Centuries before Western staff notation, Saint Yared created an indigenous notation system in Axum. Each symbol dictates vocal pitch, contour, vibrato, and breath dynamics that resonate deeply throughout Gigi's vocal stylings.

ግዕዝ (Ge'ez) Foundational, solemn chant mode representing morning prayer, clarity, and acoustic purity.
ዕዝል (Ezel) Solemn, deep, and contemplative mode invoking fasting, remembrance, and sorrowful yearning.
አራራይ (Araray) Joyous, triumphant, and ecstatic celebratory chant mode for feasts and spiritual victory.
